issues.title: Pin that the slipper's zero-width ; is never a forbidden reduce or shift on perly.y
issues.body:
## Context

- paths: internal/chart/prectab/ (a test only); internal/chart/recognize/slipper.go (read, not changed)
- commands: go test ./internal/chart/prectab/... -run '^TestSlipperSemicolon' -v
- entrypoints: the slipper's zero-width `PERLY_SEMICOLON` closure (`recognize` `Slipped`); `prectab` `ReduceAt`, `ShiftForbidden`

This carries the d199 gate's O2, per perigrin's ruling "New issue blocking d218 (Recommended)".

The slipper inserts a zero-width `;` and closes over it, and today nothing judges that closure. Its reduce half cannot refuse anything on perly.y: the d199 gate counted 0 rules with a non-allow reduce verdict before `PERLY_SEMICOLON`. Nobody has counted its shift half. Once d218 removes `Constrain` from `ParseWith`, a forbidden shift of the inserted `;` would go unjudged. This issue pins both halves on perly.y with counters before that happens.

Carries: none. This was found at the gate, not in the minute.

## Steps

- [ ] Write `TestSlipperSemicolonReduceNeverForbidden`. Over perly.y's precedence, count the rules whose reduce verdict before `PERLY_SEMICOLON` is not allow, and the rules considered. Log `semicolon reduces forbidden: F of N`. Require F to be 0 and N to be greater than 0.
- [ ] Write `TestSlipperSemicolonShiftNeverForbidden`. Over perly.y's precedence, count every (state, item) pair whose shift of `PERLY_SEMICOLON` is forbidden, out of the pairs that can shift it. Log `semicolon shifts forbidden: F of N`. Require F to be 0 and N to be greater than 0.
- [ ] Prove by mutation that each test goes red when its predicate is broken, for example by treating every verdict as forbidding. Revert each mutation.
- [ ] Run `T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit make test`, then restore `test/e2e/.perl-version`.
- [ ] Commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Positive Scenarios
- [ ] No reduce before the slipper's `;` is forbidden on perly.y (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestSlipperSemicolonReduceNeverForbidden\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: TestSlipperSemicolonReduceNeverForbidden (" || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -Eq -- "semicolon reduces forbidden: 0 of [1-9][0-9]*" || exit 1'`)
- [ ] No shift of the slipper's `;` is forbidden on perly.y (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestSlipperSemicolonShiftNeverForbidden\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: TestSlipperSemicolonShiftNeverForbidden (" || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -Eq -- "semicolon shifts forbidden: 0 of [1-9][0-9]*" || exit 1'`)

### Negative Scenarios
- [ ] Neither counter skips (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestSlipperSemicolon" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; ! printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- SKIP"'`)

## Stops

The design §7 stops apply. If either count is not 0, that is a stop. Report it to perigrin. The slipper's closure would then need judging with records Build reads beside `Slipped`. Do not weaken the counter to reach 0.

## Gate findings (reopen 1, gate at ad48bb3c, report exec/d1e6-gate.md)

- **F1 (in scope).** Two denominators are reported but cannot fail. The gate's mutation log is `d1e6-gate-mutations.log`.
  - TR (`range tab.Rules[:0]`) still PASSes with `0 of 350`, because `considered := len(tab.Rules)` is a constant.
  - TS1 (an empty `tops` slice) PASSes with `0 of 61`, because no top is ever checked.
  - TS2 (the filter narrowed to `Dot <= 1`) PASSes with `0 of 47`.

  The fix:
  1. Count `considered` inside the reduce loop.
  2. Log the number of tops, and require it to be greater than 0.
  3. Pin the populations exactly, as `TestPrectabItemMapping` does: 350 rules, 61 pairs, 46 tops.
  4. Prove by mutation that TR, TS1 and TS2 each go red, then revert them.

issues.title: Run the cost bounds on the judged recognizer, and check that its Leo walk is linear
issues.body:
## Context

- paths: internal/chart/recognize/probes_test.go; internal/chart/recognize/leo_test.go; internal/chart/recognize/judge.go, leo.go, leo_memo.go, recognize.go (the walk fix, by ruling); internal/chart/README.md
- commands: go test ./internal/chart/recognize/... -run 'Bounded|JudgedLeoWalk' -v
- entrypoints: `recognize.NewJudged`; `leoCrosses` in `recognize/judge.go`; `completionProbesBound`, `leoMemoEntriesBound`

This carries the d199 gate's O4, per perigrin's ruling "Measure before switch (Recommended)".

`TestCompletionProbesBounded` (bound 0.64) and `TestLeoMemoEntriesBounded` (bound 0.040) measure the default recognizer only. The judged recognizer's Leo step, `leoCrosses`, walks the whole memo chain on every Leo completion, so right recursion could become quadratic again there. Nothing would see that before the switch-over makes the judged recognizer the default. This issue runs the same bounds, at the same constants, on the judged recognizer, and adds a linearity check on Leo's walk.

Carries: none. This was found at the gate, not in the minute.

## Steps

- [ ] Write `TestCompletionProbesBoundedJudged` and `TestLeoMemoEntriesBoundedJudged`. Each runs the existing measurement on the derived judged recognizer over perly.y, against the existing constants, unchanged. Each logs its ratio the way its default twin does.
- [ ] Write `TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear`. On a right-recursive input that Leo handles, at two lengths n and 2n, count the memo links `leoCrosses` walks. Log `leo walk: W1 at n, W2 at 2n`. Require W2 to be at most 2.5 times W1, with W1 greater than 0.
- [ ] Prove by mutation that each new test can fail. For example, make `leoCrosses` re-walk the chain from its head on every step, and see `TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear` go red. Revert each mutation.
- [ ] Run `T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit make test`, then restore `test/e2e/.perl-version`.
- [ ] Commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Positive Scenarios
- [ ] The judged recognizer meets the completion-probe bound (`go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run '^TestCompletionProbesBoundedJudged$' -v 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestCompletionProbesBoundedJudged ('`)
- [ ] The judged recognizer meets the Leo memo bound (`go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run '^TestLeoMemoEntriesBoundedJudged$' -v 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestLeoMemoEntriesBoundedJudged ('`)
- [ ] Leo's judged walk grows linearly (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear (" || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -Eq -- "leo walk: [1-9][0-9]* at " || exit 1'`)

### Negative Scenarios
- [ ] The bounds' constants are unchanged (`grep -q 'const completionProbesBound = 0.64' internal/chart/recognize/probes_test.go && grep -q 'const leoMemoEntriesBound = 0.040' internal/chart/recognize/leo_test.go`)

## Stops

The design §7 stops apply. A red bound, or a walk that grows faster than linearly, is a stop. Report it to perigrin. Never retune a constant to make it pass.

## Gate findings (reopen 1, gate at ec1a2872, report exec/d35d-gate.md) and amendment

**STOP raised and ruled.** `TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear` cannot fail on its claim. Its toys take Leo once per input. On the shape this issue exists for, the unchanged judged code walks 4851, then 19701, then 79401 links at n = 100, 200 and 400. That is n(n−1)/2, quadratic, where the default recognizer is linear. The shape is a right-recursive nonterminal whose FOLLOW holds the token that continues it: `S ::= L T ; L ::= a L | a ; T ::= a T | b`, on input aⁿ b. No perly.y input was found with this shape.

perigrin ruled two things, on 2026-11-26:
- "Fix it in d35d (Recommended)". This issue's scope widens from tests only to a production fix that makes `leoCrosses` linear.
- "Add it with the fix (Recommended)". A corpus bound on Leo links per token is added here.

### Amended Steps
- [ ] Make the judged Leo walk linear.
  - One option is to record each memo's first refused link when the memo is built.
  - Another is to cache the crossing verdict per memo and lookahead.
  - Behaviour must stay identical: every forest-equality and reduce-side differential stays green, and the Leo-agreement tests stay green.
- [ ] Rewrite `TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear` on the gate's toy (above), or one of the same shape.
  - Log `leo steps: S1 at n, S2 at 2n` beside `leo walk: W1 at n, W2 at 2n`.
  - Require S2 > S1 > 0, so that Leo really fires at many positions.
  - Require W2 ≤ 2.5·W1.
  - On the unfixed code the test must be red. Show this by running it before the fix.
- [ ] Add `TestLeoLinksPerTokenBoundedJudged`.
  - It counts `leoLinks` per token over the same corpus sample the other bounds use, on the judged recognizer.
  - Its bound is a new constant, `leoLinksPerTokenBound`. Set it from the measured value after the fix, with the same small headroom the existing bounds carry, and log the ratio. The sample measured 58/34924 before the fix.
- [ ] Correct the README's judged-recognizer bullet (gate F3). The linearity claim must be true as stated.
- [ ] Prove by mutation that each test can fail:
  - reverting the fix turns the linearity test red;
  - inflating `leoLinks` turns the links bound red;
  - swapping in `NewNoPrecedence` changes what is measured.

### Added Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Leo's judged walk is linear where Leo fires at many positions (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear (" || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -Eq -- "leo steps: [1-9][0-9]* at [0-9]+, [1-9][0-9]* at " || exit 1'`)
- [ ] The judged recognizer meets the Leo-links bound (`go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run '^TestLeoLinksPerTokenBoundedJudged$' -v 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestLeoLinksPerTokenBoundedJudged ('`)
- [ ] The Leo-links bound is a declared constant (`grep -q 'leoLinksPerTokenBound' internal/chart/recognize/leo_test.go`)

The original criteria still apply. That includes the two existing bounds at unchanged constants.

## Gate findings (reopen 2, gate at 6d0c93f6, report exec/d35d-gate2.md)

- **G1 (in scope, STOP, within the existing ruling "Fix it in d35d").** The pass-2 fix caches one verdict per memo, keyed by the last lookahead, so the walk is still quadratic whenever the lookahead alternates. Measured with `S ::= L T; L ::= a L | b L | a | b; T ::= a T | b T | c` on (a b)ⁿ c:
  - links: 19701, 79401 and 318801 at n = 100, 200 and 400, which is n(n−1)/2;
  - with a third continuing token, 44551, 179101 and 718201.

  The README linearity claim is still false.

  **Fix.** Key the crossing verdict by lookahead class, not by the last lookahead:
  - `r.lookahead` returns a class id, or −1 for a union;
  - keep a per-memo map or slice from class to verdict, so each link is walked at most once per class;
  - keep the bitset comparison as the fallback for −1.

  **Test.** Add the alternating grammar, and the three-token variant, as cases of `TestJudgedLeoWalkLinear`:
  - require leo steps to grow and W2 ≤ 2.5·W1 in every case;
  - show each case red on 6d0c93f6, then green on the fix.

  **README.** Make the linearity sentence true as stated.
- **G2 (out of scope, folded in).** No test pins the cache key. Add a mutation that collapses the key, for example by ignoring the class, and show the alternating case goes red.

issues.title: Delete the §4.3 clause from PredictionContexts and keep forbidsAt as the test's oracle
issues.body:
## Context

- paths: internal/chart/prectab/contexts.go; internal/chart/prectab/contexts_test.go; internal/chart/README.md (the Items bullet)
- commands: go test ./internal/chart/prectab/... -run '^TestContextCollapseTable$' -v
- entrypoints: `prectab.PredictionContexts`; `forbidsAt`

This carries the d1c2 gate's F1. perigrin ruled "Delete it, keep as oracle (Recommended)".

`PredictionContexts` gives each predictor one context. At that granularity, §4.3's collapse is identical to §4.2's for every grammar. A canonical top forbids shifts only in rules predicted from it, and those rules lie in its own predictor's region. So the `forbidsAt` clause in `PredictionContexts` can never fire. It is dead code, and removing it fails no test.

The ruling says §4.3 is §4.2 at predictor granularity. A finer per-state collapse is not built: the d1c2 worker and its gate both judged it unsound under 3282's pairing, or else needing a §7 item fact.

Carries: none. This was found at the gate, not in the minute.

## Steps

- [ ] Change the README first. The Items bullet must say that at predictor granularity §4.3's collapse adds nothing to §4.2's, and why.
- [ ] Remove the `forbidsAt` clause from `PredictionContexts`. Move `forbidsAt` into `contexts_test.go`, where `TestContextCollapseTable` keeps it as the oracle checked against the brute-force witness search.
- [ ] Prove by mutation that `TestContextCollapseTable` still goes red when its predicate or its population is broken. Revert each mutation.
- [ ] Confirm that the context table is unchanged: 261 predictors, 46 keep a top, 215 collapse by §4.2.
- [ ] Run `T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit make test`, then restore `test/e2e/.perl-version`.
- [ ] Commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Positive Scenarios
- [ ] PredictionContexts no longer holds the §4.3 clause (`! grep -q 'forbidsAt' internal/chart/prectab/contexts.go`)
- [ ] The collapse table and its oracle still pass (`go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run '^TestContextCollapseTable$' -v 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestContextCollapseTable ('`)
- [ ] The README states the granularity (`grep -q 'predictor granularity' internal/chart/README.md`)

### Negative Scenarios
- [ ] The no-precedence sets are still e3432c0f's (`go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run '^TestSetDigestNoPrecedenceGolden$' -v 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--- PASS: TestSetDigestNoPrecedenceGolden ('`)

## Stops

The design §7 stops apply. If removing the clause changes any context, any set, or any forest, that is a stop.

issues.title: Walk Build's forest by context without a per-node hash map
issues.body:
## Context

- paths: internal/chart/forest/bycontext.go; internal/chart/forest/forest.go (`leoFacts`); internal/chart/forest/judged_test.go; internal/chart/README.md
- commands: T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit make test
- entrypoints: docs/assessments/chart-perly-w4/early-reading/README.md; docs/assessments/chart-precedence-v2/rulings.md (2026-11-27, "A, then re-read (Recommended)")

The early speed reading missed design §7's exit. The before-minimum was 3.2143 and the after-median 3.3991. perigrin ruled "Profile, then new issue (Recommended)", and then, on the profile, "A, then re-read (Recommended)".

**The cause.** Issue 3282 added the walk by context, `(*builder).byContext` in `forest/bycontext.go`, and `build` runs it whenever `b.walk` is set. On a judged chart `b.walk` is set in almost every file: 1597 of 2211 files in the ratchet's aggregate, holding 99.4% of its tokens.

The walk goes over the whole reachable forest a second time. It does a hash-map insert and lookup in `seen` for every (node, context) pair, and it builds the `keep` closure once per alternative. That doubles `forest.Build`, from 463 ms to 1030 ms per aggregate pass. The `seen` map alone is 27% of Build's CPU and allocates about 1.3 GB per pass.

Separately, `leoFacts` grows `b.leoAt` by `append`, which adds about 10k allocations per pass.

**This issue is direction A from the profile.** The walk keeps its visit order and its set semantics. Only its bookkeeping changes:
- Replace `seen` with a per-node `reached []bool` and the first context each node was reached under.
- Fall back to a map only when a node is reached under a second context. On the aggregate that is about 0.8% of nodes.
- Create the `keep` closure once per walk.
- Pre-size `b.leoAt` in `leoFacts`.

A prototype of this change gave byte-identical forests for all 2211 aggregate files, and Build fell to about 800 ms per pass. Allocations per token fell from 0.114 to 0.085.

The change reads nothing new: only `Item.Ctx`, which is the canonical spine top, and the refusal records Build already reads. No item fact is added, and no forest may change.

Out of scope:
- Direction B, which keeps each alternative's placed-item range or memoizes `completedUnder`. perigrin ruled A first.
- The re-reading, which the orchestrator takes after merge.

Carries: none (new, from the early reading's stop).

## Steps

- [ ] First commit: correct any `internal/chart/README.md` sentence this change makes false, for example one describing the walk's bookkeeping (live document first). Make a minimal edit only. The final docs issue owns the shared sections.
- [ ] Write `TestBuildAllocsPerTokenBoundedJudged` in package forest. It measures `forest.Build`'s allocations per token over judged charts (`recognize.New`) of the in-tree corpus sample the existing judged bounds use, and bounds them with a named constant set from the measured value after the fix. It must fail at origin/pu before the change. Record the before and after values in the commit message.
- [ ] Rewrite the walk's bookkeeping as described in Context: no per-node map, the closure hoisted, and `leoAt` pre-sized.
- [ ] Show the forests are unchanged. Every forest-equality and digest test must pass unmodified, and `resolved-forest-digest.golden` must be byte-identical to e3432c0f's.
- [ ] Mutation proof: make the walk skip the second-context fallback, so that a node reached under a second context is not revisited. A test must go red. If none does, add one that does, using a toy where a node is reached under two contexts and only the second keeps an alternative.
- [ ] Close through the prepared driver script: `T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit make test`, then restore `test/e2e/.perl-version` with `git checkout -- test/e2e/.perl-version`.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Positive Scenarios
- [ ] Build's allocations per token on judged charts are bounded and the bound test passes without skipping (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/forest -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestBuildAllocsPerTokenBoundedJudged\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: TestBuildAllocsPerTokenBoundedJudged (" || exit 1; ! printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- SKIP" || exit 1'`)
- [ ] The judged forest-equality and walk tests pass unmodified (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/forest -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^(TestBuildDropsAlternativeOfDeadContext|TestBuildReadsNoRefusedRule|TestForestEqualityJudgedRecognizer|TestForestEqualityJudgedCandidateNeverConstrains|TestForestDigestGolden|TestResolvedForestDigestGolden)\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; for t in TestBuildDropsAlternativeOfDeadContext TestBuildReadsNoRefusedRule TestForestEqualityJudgedRecognizer TestForestEqualityJudgedCandidateNeverConstrains TestForestDigestGolden TestResolvedForestDigestGolden; do printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: $t (" || exit 1; done; ! printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- SKIP" || exit 1'`)
- [ ] The corpus forest equality holds over every file (`sh -c 'out=$(T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^TestForestEqualityCorpusJudgedRecognizer\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: TestForestEqualityCorpusJudgedRecognizer (" || exit 1; ! printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- SKIP" || exit 1'`)

### Negative Scenarios
A change that moves any forest is a design §7 stop: report it, do not adjust the golden.
- [ ] resolved-forest-digest.golden is byte-identical to e3432c0f's (`git diff --quiet e3432c0f -- internal/chart/forest/testdata/resolved-forest-digest.golden`)
- [ ] No golden or testdata file under internal/chart changes in this issue's range (`sh -c 'base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/pu); ! git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD -- internal/chart | grep -q testdata/'`)
- [ ] The existing judged cost bounds still pass (`sh -c 'out=$(go test ./internal/chart/... -count=1 -timeout 1800s -run "^(TestCompletionProbesBoundedJudged|TestLeoMemoEntriesBoundedJudged|TestLeoLinksPerTokenBoundedJudged)\$" -v 2>&1) || exit 1; for t in TestCompletionProbesBoundedJudged TestLeoMemoEntriesBoundedJudged TestLeoLinksPerTokenBoundedJudged; do printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -q -- "--- PASS: $t (" || exit 1; done'`)

## README step

If no README sentence describes the walk's bookkeeping, make no README edit, and say so in the report. Otherwise make one minimal edit.

## Stops

Design §7's stops apply. Report each of these with evidence, and never tune toward or work around it:
- any forest differs;
- a golden moves;
- an answer key moves;
- a fix would need an item fact beyond the canonical spine top;
- a criterion would need changing.

## Reopen 1 (gate 4792-gate.md, TIER_2, runner 4792-run at f65f598a)

- **F1 (in scope):** the mutation proof does not hold.
  - The gate made the walk never revisit a node under a second context. Every test in forest, chart and cmd/ratchet stayed green, with `T1_CORPUS` set correctly and without it.
  - The red `TestResolveKeepsCorpusAccepted` the worker saw came from a wrong `T1_CORPUS` path (`/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava`). That test lives in package forest, not chart.
  - So the Step applies as written. Add a toy where a node is reached under two contexts and only the second keeps an alternative.
  - The test must go red under the mutation and green at the fix. Always set `T1_CORPUS=/opt/corpora/PerlOnJava/src/test/resources/unit` explicitly.
- **F2 (in scope, minor):** the comment on `buildAllocsPerTokenBound` gives the before value as 0.5268. The measured value is 0.5264, as the commit message says.
